lines.note: Ichiracu is explained as one pleasure or enjoyment, matching Fitotçuno tanoximi. The Portuguese begins a pair of near-synonyms completed below.
Ou prazer completes the gloss as pleasure or delight; this short continuation is a separate physical line.
Ichiracu sacu denotes settling or determining a dispute. The Portuguese divides sobre at the visible line-end hyphen.
The determination concerns a lawsuit or claim; Ichiracu sacuno begins a temporal expression continued with aida below.
Aida completes 'while the matter is being settled'. The scan supports conclue and an ampersand, rather than OCR condue; the Portuguese also mentions investigating or ascertaining the claim.
A demanda supplies the object of conclue and auerigua above: the dispute being resolved, not a new entry.
This Ichiran is a disturbance or revolt, distinct from the homophonous viewing term in the next entry.
The second Ichiran means one look or inspection. Its example begins the deferential verb tçucamatçuru across the physical line break.

runs.text: Ver de hũa vez, ou leuemẽte.

lines.note: Matçuru completes the verb in Ichiran tçucamatçuru; the Portuguese explains taking one look or looking cursorily. The abbreviation tilde in leuemẽte is retained.
Ichirei, explained by Fitotçuno rei, is one act of courtesy or reverence; the gloss continues below.
Ichireiuo mǒſu illustrates making a respectful salutation. The Japanese mǒſu is upright, while Vt and Fazer belong to the italic apparatus.
Completes Fazer with one reverence or courtesy, confirming the salutation sense rather than a numerical rule.
Ichiri is one reason or argument. The Japanese explanatory cotouari has r, not the OCR's t, consistent with the Portuguese rezão.
Arrezoamento completes the alternative gloss as reasoning or an argument. Its historical spelling is preserved.
Ichirin is first defined as one wheel or circle; the following Item introduces a transferred use of that circular image.
Per met introduces the moon or sun as a disc. Ichirin tacacu begins the example about that disc being high in the sky.
Cacareba completes the condition 'when it hangs high'; bancocu vonajicu miru says that all countries see it alike. Eſtã- begins the Portuguese rendering on this row.

runs.text: do o ſol, ou lũa alta, de todos os Reinos o

lines.note: Do completes Eſtãdo, describing the sun or moon high above and visible from all kingdoms; the final o anticipates the object of vem below.
Completes the comparison: people see it in the same way. Final S is the upright written-register label, not part of the italic sentence.
Ichiriǒxo means one or two places. The internal r corrects OCR t; the marked o belongs to the ryo element, not a separate malformed syllable.
Ichiriqi is one person's strength or resources, explicitly equated with Fitotçuno chicara. The headword begins with a capital I in the scan.
The gloss specifies the strength of one alone; Ichiriqide xita co- begins 'a thing done by one's own resources'. Two o types are visible in ſoo.

runs.text: He couſa que eu fiz com minhas forças,

lines.note: Togia completes cotogia, 'it is a thing that ...'. The Portuguese makes the subject first person: something I did with my own strength.

runs.text: ou com meu poder, & de meus criados.

lines.note: The explanatory alternatives include the person's power and that of his servants. This qualifies 'alone' as one's own household resources, not necessarily unassisted physical effort.
Ichiriǔ manbai expresses ten thousandfold return from a single grain. The Portuguese hum has the same italic h shape seen elsewhere, not OCR bum.
Ichiriǔ manbaino miuo toru illustrates receiving the fruit of that multiplication. The Japanese example repeats the headword's marked u.

runs.text: fruito, ou proueito de mil, ou dez mil por hũ

lines.note: The Portuguese states a yield or benefit of a thousand or ten thousand for one; the compressed hũ belongs with grão on the next row.
Grão de ſemente completes the image of one seed producing a great return. The source's singular grain remains explicit.
Ichiro is one road or way, as the Japanese michi and Portuguese caminho agree. Preserve the capital I and the upright written-register S.
Ichirô is a single elevated structure, explained by yagura and Portuguese baileu; its circumflex distinguishes this from the unmarked road entry above.
The continuation describes a high storey or platform like a small tower. The scan retains the n in torreſinha, absent from the OCR draft.
Ichirui means one kind or class, with taguy as its Japanese explanation. The comma after eſpecia connects to the alternative on the next line.
Ou laya completes the classifying gloss as a kind or sort. It belongs to Ichirui above, not the house entry below.
Ichiv here means one house, with iye making the sense explicit. The worn initial is I, not OCR A; the final v is retained as printed.
The next Ichiv is homophonous but means one rainfall or shower, explained by Fitoame and chuua.
Ichiun means one cloud, with cumo confirming the noun. The capital initial and nuuem's historical spelling are preserved.
Ichiuǒ is glossed as once, with Fitotçu yucu supplying its Japanese explanation. The example begins Ichi at the right edge without an added hyphen.
Uǒ completes the divided example headword; mǒsǒ means 'I shall say'. Enlargement shows a worn round s between the marked vowels, not OCR e and not a tall long-s type.
This Ichiyacu is one medicine or remedy, explicitly equated with cuſuri. The medical example continues below.
Ichiyacuuo xubiǒni atǒru illustrates applying one remedy to many illnesses. The marked vowels in the Japanese are retained rather than normalized from modern pronunciation.
Completes Dar hũa mezinha as giving one remedy for all illnesses; this is the dictionary's example, not an endorsement of a medical claim.
A different Ichiyacu means one office or duty, as yacu and officio indicate. It is independent of the medicine entry.
The third Ichiyacu denotes one promise or agreement, made explicit by yacuſocu. The Portuguese pro- continues on the next physical row.
Meßa completes promeßa, followed by concerto in the sense of an agreement. The printed beta-like doubled-s form is retained from the aligned draft.
Ichiye is one garment, corresponding to coromo. The Portuguese veſtido describes clothing, not a household.
Ichiyei denotes prosperity or flourishing, with ſacaye as its Japanese explanation. The entry has a capital I and divides proſperidade across the row boundary.
Dade completes proſperidade. The example juxtaposes flourishing and falling away as something plainly before one's eyes; its Portuguese explanation begins at the top of the second column.

runs.text: A proſperidade que logo ſe muda, he ma-

lines.note: Continues the preceding column's Ichiyei example: prosperity changes immediately. The predicate 'is manifest' is divided across this and the next row.
Nifesta completes manifesta, saying that the changeability of prosperity is plain. The source's physical division ma-/nifesta is preserved.
This Ichiyei concerns an eye-film or discharge, glossed remela and explained by maqe. It is a separate homophone from prosperity.
The example says that when even one obstruction is in the eye, illusory flowers appear to fall through the air. The literal Japanese image explains the more general Portuguese paraphrase below.

runs.text: Auendo remela, ou humidade nos olhos

lines.note: The concluding ſu completes the Japanese example. Portuguese Auendo introduces the condition of discharge or moisture in the eyes.

runs.text: faz parecer o que não he. S.

lines.note: The condition makes something nonexistent appear to be present, completing the visual-illusion example. Final S is an upright written-register label.
Ichiyen is identified as an adverb meaning 'in no way' when used with a negative; the grammatical qualification continues below.

runs.text: ſe ajunta com negatiuo. ¶ Item, Em todo

lines.note: Completes the negative-construction qualification and introduces a second, affirmative sense with Item: 'in any case'.
The second use is illustrated by Ichiyenni cono cotouo tçuca-, beginning a statement of resolve to perform this particular act.
Matçurǒzu completes the prospective verb. The Portuguese says 'this alone I shall do', clarifying the emphatic rather than negative use.
Ichiyeqi, explained as Fitotçu maſu, is an increase or surplus. The Portuguese alternative continues on the next row.
Ventajem completes the gloss as advantage or gain; its historical j spelling is retained.

runs.text: Palaura que às vezes ſe toma por ſol,

lines.note: This Ichiyǒ can signify the sun, with the explanation expressly saying that these are occasional uses of the word.

runs.text: ou quentura, ou prima vera. S.

lines.note: Warmth and spring complete the listed senses. Preserve the visible separation prima vera and the upright written-register S.
The next Ichiyǒ means one form or manner, corresponding to Fitoſama, rather than the preceding seasonal term.
Ichiyǒni xitacu ſuru means preparing or equipping oneself in the same manner. The Portuguese da is completed by meſma maneira below.
Meſma maneira completes the preceding example as preparing in an identical fashion. The short line closes that entry.
Ichiyô, with a circumflex, means one leaf, explicitly explained by Fitofa. The following entry line adds a literary vessel sense.
The printed pilcrow introduces the additional sense 'a boat or vessel'. Final S marks written usage; both the omitted pilcrow and upright label are restored.
Ichizocu here denotes a family or body of relatives. The Portuguese parentella supports the kinship sense.
Icqe, ichizocu gives the paired household-and-family expression and labels it Idem, equivalent to the preceding definition.
A distinct homophone Ichizocu means one layperson, glossed secular, rather than a family collectively.
The third Ichizocu means a single thief, made unambiguous by Fitorino nuſubito and ladrão.
Ichizzu is explained by Fitomichi, a single way. The Portuguese begins a broader gloss covering a path, habit, or manner of life; the capital I is visible.
Tume completes coſtume. The example Ichizzuna mo- starts a description of a person steadfast in a chosen course.
No completes mono. The Portuguese describes someone constant and firm in an activity or habit, continued below.
Obra and costume complete the domains in which that person is steadfast. The aligned short-s spelling in costume is retained rather than imposing a general s/ſ normalization on the compact st type.
Ichizzumi is glossed as 'in no way'. The example headword breaks after Ichiz without a visible terminal hyphen, which is not supplied.
Zumi completes Ichizzumi; iy qiru means saying decisively. The Portuguese explicitly frames a resolute refusal, completed by the next line.
Nenhũa maneira completes the emphatic 'by no means' construction. The nasal abbreviation is retained.
Ichô is identified simply as the kingdom of China; the printed circumflex is retained without modernizing the name.
Ichocu is explained by Chocu tagǒ, disobeying an imperial command. The Portuguese divides mandado after man without an added hyphen.
Dado completes mandado, the king's command that is disobeyed. The short line closes Ichocu.
Icô is 'a different mouth'. The example begins Icô dô and continues with uonni yǔ; the Japanese forms are wholly upright, not partly italic as in the OCR.
Together with dô above, uonni gives dōon ni, speaking with one voice despite different mouths. The worn final verb reads yǔ, not OCR y..; the Portuguese specifies many people praising the same thing.
Por diuerſas bocas completes the image of shared praise from different mouths. It does not introduce a second meaning of Icô.
This Icô concerns a physician's skill or experience, explained by Cuſuxino cô. Final S is the upright written-register label.

Another Icô is a clothes pole, explained by Coromo zauo; r replaces the draft's x. The dark mark over q in q̃ue is retained as the chosen reading, following the aligned draft, although the blot does not securely distinguish a tilde from an imperfect impression or stain.
Durão completes dependurão: clothes are hung on the bamboo pole. The split is preserved rather than joining the Portuguese word.
Icocu means another country, explained by Cotonaru cuni. The Portuguese offers another kingdom or a kingdom of foreigners.
De estrangeiros completes the second alternative. The supplied short-s/ligature classification is retained without a global normalization.
Icoi denotes resting. The regional note introduces Yocoi as the Ximo form, and the scan ends this line with a comma rather than the draft's period.
Yocoi, with its principal parts, is the regional alternative and is glossed as resting or sleeping. These forms are not a new independent geographical entry.

runs.text: Eſtrangeiro, ou homẽ de outro reino.

lines.note: Icocujin is a foreigner or person from another kingdom, transparently related to Icocu above. The Portuguese nasal abbreviation in homẽ is retained.
Icogi describes a guarded or evasive person. The Portuguese adjective is the continuous word refolhado, not the draft's re folhado; the historical principal part zzuru is retained.

runs.text: não ſe deixar entender por não falar a propoſi-

lines.note: The description continues: he does not let himself be understood because he does not speak directly or to the point. Propoſi- continues below.

runs.text: to nem direito, ſe não por rodeos, &c. ¶

lines.note: To completes propoſito; the person speaks in circumlocutions instead of plainly. The pilcrow starts the divided example Icogita fito, whose gita resumes as body text on f262; bottom gita is a catchword, not another body line.
